### Fixed
- **The model-serving pod policies match `LLMInferenceService` workload pods** (giantswarm/agent-platform#506): the connectivity chart's `model-serving` Kyverno mutations (`redirect-model-storage`, `storage-initializer-memory`, `add-cache-init`, the Deployments' `progress-deadline`), its network policies and the predictors' PolicyException selected pods by `serving.kserve.io/inferenceservice`, the classic `InferenceService` predictor's label; the workload pod the llm-d controller creates from an `LLMInferenceService` carries `kserve.io/component=workload`, `app.kubernetes.io/part-of=llminferenceservice` and `app.kubernetes.io/name=<model>` instead and serves from a container named `main`, so none of it applied — on gazelle (4.28.8, proof 1 of giantswarm/giantswarm#37639) the predictor composed from `qwen3-4b-instruct` downloaded 8 GB into an emptyDir with its `storage-initializer` OOMKilled twelve times at KServe's 1Gi default, while the policies stood `Ready` beside it. The two pod shapes are one list now (`agent-platform.modelServing.podShapes`: selector, model-name label, runtime container), and every selector of the serving namespace renders from it: the mutations match both shapes, take the model's name from whichever label the pod carries (the cache subdirectory), anchor the `/mnt/models` cache mount on the shape's runtime container (`kserve-container` or `main`; an anchored entry never adds a container) and skip a pod that names no model; the network policies render one policy per shape (`-model-serving-llmisvc-workload[-ingress|-egress]` next to `-predictor…`) and the kagent agents' egress admits both; the PolicyException matches both shapes' Pods, ReplicaSets and Deployments by label next to the `*-kserve*` name. `make verify-model-serving-policies` (`tests/verify-model-serving-policies.py`) runs `kyverno apply` of the rendered policies over a fixture pod of each shape (`tests/fixtures/model-serving-*-pod.yaml`, the llm-d one as observed on gazelle) and asserts the claim mount and subPath on the initializer and the runtime, the 4Gi limit, `hf-cache-init` first, a pod without an initializer and a download-Job pod untouched, the Deployments' deadline, and that the network policies, the agents' egress and the PolicyException select exactly the same pods; the CI job installs the kyverno CLI for it. The live half — the workload pod's volumes on a GPU cluster and a second load of the same preset downloading nothing — is the proof's.
